summary_paragraph: A 30-year-old woman with Type 1 diabetes and gastroparesis s/p gastric pacer was readmitted for severe nausea and bilious vomiting, just two days after a prior discharge. She was unable to tolerate oral intake or medications. Initial management included IV fluids and antiemetics, but hyponatremia developed, reaching a nadir of 128, attributed to SIADH from prolonged vomiting; this resolved with fluid restriction. Blood and urine cultures were negative, and leukocytosis was deemed stress-related. A chest X-ray showed no pulmonary cause for hyponatremia. An upper endoscopy revealed acute esophagitis, with no gastric abnormalities. Her gastric pacer was readjusted, leading to symptom improvement and tolerance of solid foods. Hypertension persisted during admission, prompting an increase in lisinopril to 10 mg daily and discontinuation of the clonidine patch due to its nausea-inducing side effects. She was discharged home in stable condition on optimized antiemetic and acid-suppression therapy, with follow-up scheduled for pacer evaluation and primary care management of blood pressure.
problems: Diabetes with neurological manifestations, type I [juvenile type], not stated as uncontrolled
